text: The normal PET/CT scan is extremely unusual given the massive lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly seen on the CTs, which raises the possibility of a "cold" lymphoma or a localized infection mimicking malignancy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Tuberculosis (disseminated/miliary)
The clinical picture of supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and severe B-symptoms, combined with the patient's explicit confirmation that a previous physician identified this as "typical" for tuberculosis, strongly supports this diagnosis despite the normal PET scan and ACE levels. I recommend initiating anti-tubercular therapy immediately.
